title: Things I built. Things I actually care about.

items.title: SprintDesk
items.overview: Software teams have no shortage of sprint tracking tools, but many are too heavy or too disconnected from where the actual work happens. Engineers lose context moving between GitHub, Jira, Slack, and their calendar. I built SprintDesk as a lightweight, real-time Kanban tracker that brings the right context into one place without asking people to change how they already work.
responsibilities: Built a task management app using React 19, TypeScript, and Supabase with a drag-and-drop Kanban board and full sprint cycle tracking.
Designed the component system in Figma before writing code, then used specification-driven prompting with GitHub Copilot to implement directly from design specs.
Built real-time sync with Supabase Realtime so changes appear instantly across users without a refresh.
Implemented per-user data isolation through row-level security so users only see and interact with their own tasks and boards.
Built an activity log recording every task move and update for auditability.
Integrated MCP to connect GitHub, Jira, Slack, and Google Calendar into one workspace.

items.title: Cue
items.overview: Coordinating music rehearsals through group chats creates missed updates, unclear ownership, and too much manual follow-up. As a singer who has dealt with that firsthand, I built Cue as a real-time collaborative platform for musicians to coordinate rehearsals, manage session roles, and sync practice schedules across performers.
responsibilities: Ran user interviews, surveys, and competitor analysis, then synthesized findings into personas and empathy maps to define information architecture, navigation flows, and interaction patterns.
Validated high-fidelity Figma prototypes through usability testing and cognitive walkthroughs before writing code.
Made design decisions grounded in HCI principles including recognition over recall, progressive disclosure, and error prevention.

Set up the TypeScript, React, Node.js, and Supabase stack from scratch using Claude Code, owning architecture decisions across Context API state management, role-awareness, and real-time session sync.
Added usability, unit, and end-to-end test coverage around the core rehearsal coordination flows.

items.title: Hearing the Battle: How Dynamic Game Audio Shapes Gameplay Experience
items.overview: Mobile Legends: Bang Bang changes battle music during high-pressure gameplay moments, and those audio shifts can shape player emotion, decisions, perceived momentum, pressure, intensity, and flow. This study examines adaptive battle music as a real-time feedback system from a UX and HCI perspective.
responsibilities: Designing an HCI research framework and observational dataset to study how adaptive battle music affects player emotion, decisions, and perceived momentum.
Tracking battle BGM changes during gameplay events including kills, enemy wipes, comeback moments, and high-pressure fights.
Applying reflexive thematic analysis to surface patterns in how sound, rhythm, and emotional pressure interact during matches.
Approaching the research as both a long-term ranked competitive player and a formally trained classical singer, bringing a rare dual lens to the study.
Exploring how adaptive battle music functions as an unspoken feedback layer during matches.
